# lib/handler_registry.rb
require_relative "handlers/log_handler"
require_relative "handlers/alert_handler"
require_relative "handlers/metric_handler"

module EventProcessor
  class HandlerRegistry
    BUILT_IN = {
      "log"    => Handlers::LogHandler,
      "alert"  => Handlers::AlertHandler,
      "metric" => Handlers::MetricHandler
    }.freeze

    def initialize
      @handlers = {}
    end

    def register(name, handler_class, config: {})
      @handlers[name.to_s] = handler_class.new(name: name.to_s, config: config)
      self
    end

    def register_from_config(handler_configs)
      handler_configs.each do |name, cfg|
        klass = BUILT_IN[name]
        next warn("Unknown handler type: #{name}") unless klass

        register(name, klass, config: cfg)
      end
      self
    end

    def get(name)
      @handlers.fetch(name.to_s) do
        raise ArgumentError, "No handler registered: #{name}"
      end
    end

    def names = @handlers.keys
    def count = @handlers.size

    def inspect
      "#<HandlerRegistry handlers=#{names.join(', ')}>"
    end
  end
end

```ruby
# lib/event_processor.rb
require_relative "config_parser"
require_relative "event"
require_relative "handler_registry"

module EventProcessor
  class Processor
    attr_reader :config, :registry, :stats

    def initialize(config_path)
      @parser   = ConfigParser.new(config_path)
      @config   = @parser.parse
      @registry = HandlerRegistry.new.register_from_config(@config.handler_config)
      @stats    = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = { processed: 0, filtered: 0, errors: 0 } }
      @dead_letter = []
    end

    # Process a single event
    def process(event)
      event_cfg = @config.events_config[event.type]

"""Custom exception hierarchy for the analytics pipeline."""

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Any


class PipelineError(Exception):
    """Base exception for all pipeline errors."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, details: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.details = details or {}


class StageError(PipelineError):
    """Raised when a pipeline stage fails."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        stage_name: str,
        message: str,
        original_error: Exception | None = None,
        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        full_message = f"Stage '{stage_name}' failed: {message}"
        super().__init__(full_message, details)
        self.stage_name = stage_name
        self.original_error = original_error


class ValidationError(PipelineError):
    """Raised when data validation fails."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        field: str,
        message: str,
        violations: list[str] | None = None,
        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        full_message = f"Validation failed for '{field}': {message}"
        super().__init__(full_message, details)
        self.field = field
        self.violations = violations or []


class ConfigurationError(PipelineError):
    """Raised when pipeline configuration is invalid."""
    pass


class RetryExhaustedError(StageError):
    """Raised when all retry attempts for a stage are exhausted."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        stage_name: str,
        attempts: int,
        last_error: Exception,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            stage_name=stage_name,
            message=f"All {attempts} retry attempts exhausted",
            original_error=last_error,
            details={"attempts": attempts},
        )
        self.attempts = attempts
        self.last_error = last_error

"""Pipeline execution context — carries data and metadata between stages."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
import uuid
from copy import deepcopy
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd


class PipelineStatus(str, Enum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    RUNNING = "running"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"


@dataclass
class StageResult:
    """Records the outcome of a single stage execution."""

    stage_name: str
    status: PipelineStatus
    duration_seconds: float
    input_row_count: int | None = None
    output_row_count: int | None = None
    error: str | None = None
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


class PipelineContext:
    """
    Mutable context object threaded through every pipeline stage.

    Holds the working DataFrame, accumulated metadata, per-stage results,
    and a shared key-value store for inter-stage communication.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        data: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        run_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.run_id: str = run_id or str(uuid.uuid4())
        self.data: pd.DataFrame = data if data is not None else pd.DataFrame()
        self.metadata: dict[str, Any] = metadata or {}
        self.stage_results: list[StageResult] = []
        self.status: PipelineStatus = PipelineStatus.PENDING
        self.start_time: float | None = None
        self.end_time: float | None = None
        self._store: dict[str, Any] = {}

    # -- key/value store for inter-stage data ----------------------------------

    def set(self, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
        """Store a value that subsequent stages can retrieve."""
        self._store[key] = value

    def get(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
        """Retrieve a previously stored value."""
        return self._store.get(key, default)

    def has(self, key: str) -> bool:
        return key in self._store

    # -- stage bookkeeping -----------------------------------------------------

    def record_stage(self, result: StageResult) -> None:
        self.stage_results.append(result)

    @property
    def row_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.data) if self.data is not None else 0

    @property
    def column_names(self) -> list[str]:
        return list(self.data.columns) if self.data is not None else []

    @property
    def total_duration(self) -> float | None:
        if self.start_time and self.end_time:
            return self.end_time - self.start_time
        return None

    # -- lifecycle helpers -----------------------------------------------------

    def mark_started(self) -> None:
        self.status = PipelineStatus.RUNNING
        self.start_time = time.time()

    def mark_completed(self) -> None:
        self.status = PipelineStatus.COMPLETED
        self.end_time = time.time()

    def mark_failed(self, error: str) -> None:
        self.status = PipelineStatus.FAILED
        self.end_time = time.time()
        self.metadata["error"] = error

    def snapshot(self) -> PipelineContext:
        """Return a deep copy — useful for branching or debugging."""
        ctx = PipelineContext(
            data=self.data.copy(deep=True) if self.data is not None else None,
            metadata=deepcopy(self.metadata),
            run_id=self.run_id,
        )
        ctx.stage_results = deepcopy(self.stage_results)
        ctx.status = self.status
        ctx.start_time = self.start_time
        ctx.end_time = self.end_time
        ctx._store = deepcopy(self._store)
        return ctx

    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "run_id": self.run_id,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "total_duration": self.total_duration,
            "row_count": self.row_count,
            "stages_executed": len(self.stage_results),
            "stages": [
                {
                    "name": r.stage_name,
                    "status": r.status.value,
                    "duration": round(r.duration_seconds, 4),
                    "rows_in": r.input_row_count,
                    "rows_out": r.output_row_count,
                }
                for r in self.stage_results
            ],
        }

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"PipelineContext(run_id={self.run_id!r}, "
            f"status={self.status.value!r}, rows={self.row_count})"
        )

"""Abstract base classes for synchronous and asynchronous pipeline stages."""

from __future__ import annotations

import abc
import asyncio
import time
import logging
from typing import Any

from analytics_pipeline.core.context import PipelineContext, PipelineStatus, StageResult
from analytics_pipeline.core.exceptions import StageError, RetryExhaustedError

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Stage(abc.ABC):
    """
    Synchronous pipeline stage.

    Subclass this and implement ``process`` to define stage logic.
    The framework wraps each call with timing, error handling and
    optional retry logic.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str | None = None,
        retries: int = 0,
        retry_delay: float = 1.0,
        config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.name: str = name or self.__class__.__name__
        self.retries = retries
        self.retry_delay = retry_delay
        self.config: dict[str, Any] = config or {}

    @abc.abstractmethod
    def process(self, context: PipelineContext) -> PipelineContext:
        """Override with stage-specific logic.  Must return the context."""
        ...

    def validate_input(self, context: PipelineContext) -> None:
        """Optional pre-condition check (override as needed)."""
        pass

    def validate_output(self, context: PipelineContext) -> None:
        """Optional post-condition check (override as needed)."""
        pass

    def execute(self, context: PipelineContext) -> PipelineContext:
        """
        Public entry-point called by the pipeline runner.

        Handles validation → process → validation with timing and retries.
        """
        input_rows = context.row_count
        start = time.time()
        last_error: Exception | None = None

        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 2):  # +2 ⇒ first try + retries
            try:
                logger.info(
                    "Stage %s: attempt %d/%d started",
                    self.name, attempt, self.retries + 1,
                )
                self.validate_input(context)
                context = self.process(context)
                self.validate_output(context)

                duration = time.time() - start
                context.record_stage(
                    StageResult(
                        stage_name=self.name,
                        status=PipelineStatus.COMPLETED,
                        duration_seconds=duration,
                        input_row_count=input_rows,
                        output_row_count=context.row_count,
                    )
                )
                logger.info(
                    "Stage %s: completed in %.3fs (%d→%d rows)",
                    self.name, duration, input_rows, context.row_count,
                )
                return context

            except Exception as exc:
                last_error = exc
                logger.warning(
                    "Stage %s: attempt %d failed — %s",
                    self.name, attempt, exc,
                )
                if attempt <= self.retries:
                    time.sleep(self.retry_delay)

        # all attempts exhausted
        duration = time.time() - start
        context.record_stage(
            StageResult(
                stage_name=self.name,
                status=PipelineStatus.FAILED,
                duration_seconds=duration,
                input_row_count=input_rows,
                error=str(last_error),
            )
        )
        raise RetryExhaustedError(
            stage_name=self.name,
            attempts=self.retries + 1,
            last_error=last_error,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        )

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.__class__.__name__}(name={self.name!r})"


class AsyncStage(abc.ABC):
    """Async variant of :class:`Stage` for I/O-bound workloads."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str | None = None,
        retries: int = 0,
        retry_delay: float = 1.0,
        config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.name: str = name or self.__class__.__name__
        self.retries = retries
        self.retry_delay = retry_delay
        self.config: dict[str, Any] = config or {}

    @abc.abstractmethod
    async def process(self, context: PipelineContext) -> PipelineContext:
        ...

    async def validate_input(self, context: PipelineContext) -> None:
        pass

    async def validate_output(self, context: PipelineContext) -> None:
        pass

    async def execute(self, context: PipelineContext) -> PipelineContext:
        input_rows = context.row_count
        start = time.time()
        last_error: Exception | None = None

        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 2):
            try:
                await self.validate_input(context)
                context = await self.process(context)
                await self.validate_output(context)

                duration = time.time() - start
                context.record_stage(
                    StageResult(
                        stage_name=self.name,
                        status=PipelineStatus.COMPLETED,
                        duration_seconds=duration,
                        input_row_count=input_rows,
                        output_row_count=context.row_count,
                    )
                )
                return context

            except Exception as exc:
                last_error = exc
                if attempt <= self.retries:
                    await asyncio.sleep(self.retry_delay)

        duration = time.time() - start
        context.record_stage(
            StageResult(
                stage_name=self.name,
                status=PipelineStatus.FAILED,
                duration_seconds=duration,
                input_row_count=input_rows,
                error=str(last_error),
            )
        )
        raise RetryExhaustedError(
            stage_name=self.name,
            attempts=self.retries + 1,
            last_error=last_error,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        )

# ─── Failure hierarchy ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Failure modes (see § Failure Modes at the bottom for the full table):
#
#   ConfigError            – catch-all for parse-time problems
#   ├─ SchemaViolation     – required field missing / wrong type
#   ├─ InvalidValue        – value parses but is semantically wrong
#   PoisonPillQuarantined  – message exceeded max redeliveries
#   QueueOverflow          – queue depth ≥ configured max

class ConfigError(Exception):
    """Base for every config-parse failure."""


class SchemaViolation(ConfigError):
    """A required key is absent or has the wrong type."""


class InvalidValue(ConfigError):
    """The value parsed, but it is out of range or semantically wrong."""


class PoisonPillQuarantined(Exception):
    """Raised when a message is shunted to the dead-letter quarantine."""


class QueueOverflow(Exception):
    """Raised when the in-memory queue exceeds its depth limit."""


# ─── Config data models (all frozen → immutable after parse) ──────────

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RetryPolicy:
    max_attempts: int = 5
    backoff_base_seconds: float = 1.0
    backoff_max_seconds: float = 60.0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.max_attempts < 1:
            raise InvalidValue(
                f"retry.max_attempts must be ≥ 1, got {self.max_attempts}"
            )
        if self.backoff_base_seconds <= 0:
            raise InvalidValue(
                f"retry.backoff_base_seconds must be > 0, "
                f"got {self.backoff_base_seconds}"
            )
        if self.backoff_max_seconds < self.backoff_base_seconds:
            raise InvalidValue(
                f"retry.backoff_max_seconds ({self.backoff_max_seconds}) "
                f"< backoff_base_seconds ({self.backoff_base_seconds})"
            )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PoisonPillPolicy:
    """Controls when a repeatedly-failing message gets quarantined."""
    max_redeliveries: int = 10
    quarantine_enabled: bool = True
    alert_on_quarantine: bool = True

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.max_redeliveries < 1:
            raise InvalidValue(
                f"poison_pill.max_redeliveries must be ≥ 1, "
                f"got {self.max_redeliveries}"
            )


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class WebhookEndpoint:
    url: str
    method: str = "POST"
    timeout_seconds: float = 30.0
    headers: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()   # frozen-friendly

// Design: every error the system can reasonably encounter at runtime is an

export class OperationalError extends Error {
  /** @param {string} message
   *  @param {{ code?: string, cause?: Error, metadata?: object }} opts */
  constructor(message, opts = {}) {
    super(message, { cause: opts.cause });
    this.name        = new.target.name;   // inherits subclass name
    this.code        = opts.code ?? 'ERR_OPERATIONAL';
    this.operational = true;               // sentinel for catch-all handlers
    this.metadata    = Object.freeze(opts.metadata ?? {});
    Error.captureStackTrace?.(this, new.target);
  }

  /** Safe for structured logging (no circular refs). */
  toJSON() {
    return {
      name:     this.name,
      code:     this.code,
      message:  this.message,
      metadata: this.metadata,
      ...(this.cause && { cause: String(this.cause) }),

  }

### `src/persistence/atomic-writer.mjs` — The Fix for Partial Writes

```js
// src/persistence/atomic-writer.mjs
//
// FIX: write to temp file → datasync → rename.
//
// Why this works:
//   • rename(2) is atomic on POSIX when src and dst share a mount.
//   • datasync ensures bytes hit non-volatile storage before the rename.
//   • If the process crashes during write, only the temp file is damaged;
//     the previous checkpoint is still intact at the canonical path.
//
// Tradeoffs:
//   • datasync adds ~1–4 ms per call on SSD, ~8–15 ms on HDD.
//     Batching checkpoints amortizes this cost (see worker.mjs).
//   • On Windows, rename is NOT atomic.  We detect Windows and fall back
//     to a copy+rename pattern that is mostly-safe but not crash-proof.

import { open, rename, unlink, readFile, access, readdir } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { randomBytes, createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { dirname, join, basename } from 'node:path';
import { constants } from 'node:fs';
import { PartialWriteError, CheckpointCorruptError, OperationalError } from '../errors.mjs';

const IS_WIN = process.platform === 'win32';
const TEMP_PREFIX = '.ckpt_tmp_';

export class AtomicWriter {
  /** @type {Set<string>} tracks in-flight temp files for shutdown cleanup */
  #pending = new Set();

  /**
   * Atomically write `data` to `targetPath`.
   *
   * Failure modes this handles:
   *   F1  Process crash during write      → temp file orphaned, target intact
   *   F2  Disk full during write          → temp cleaned up, error thrown
   *   F3  Permission denied               → error thrown immediately
   *   F4  datasync failure (I/O error)    → temp cleaned up, error thrown
   *   F5  rename failure (cross-device)   → temp cleaned up, error thrown
   *   F6  Partial write (bytesWritten < expected) → detected and thrown
   */
  async write(targetPath, data) {
    const payload   = typeof data === 'string' ? data : JSON.stringify(data);
    const buf       = Buffer.from(payload, 'utf8');
    const checksum  = createHash('sha256').update(buf).digest('hex');
    // Envelope: checksum + newline + payload.  The reader verifies the checksum
    // to detect corruption that rename alone cannot prevent (e.g. bit-rot).
    const envelope  = Buffer.concat([
      Buffer.from(checksum + '\n', 'ascii'),
      buf,
    ]);

    const dir      = dirname(targetPath);
    const nonce    = randomBytes(6).toString('hex');
    const tempPath = join(dir, `${TEMP_PREFIX}${process.pid}_${nonce}`);

    this.#pending.add(tempPath);
    let fd;

    try {
      fd = await open(tempPath, 'w', 0o644);

      const { bytesWritten } = await fd.write(envelope, 0, envelope.byteLength, 0);
      if (bytesWritten !== envelope.byteLength) {
        throw new PartialWriteError(tempPath, bytesWritten, envelope.byteLength);
      }

      // datasync flushes file data (not metadata like mtime) to the device.
      // This is cheaper than fsync and sufficient for our integrity guarantee.
      await fd.datasync();
      await fd.close();
      fd = null;

      await rename(tempPath, targetPath);
      this.#pending.delete(tempPath);

      return { bytesWritten: envelope.byteLength, checksum };
    } catch (err) {
      if (fd) await fd.close().catch(() => {});
      await unlink(tempPath).catch(() => {});
      this.#pending.delete(tempPath);

      if (err instanceof OperationalError) throw err;

      throw new OperationalError(`Atomic write to ${targetPath} failed`, {
        code: 'ERR_ATOMIC_WRITE',
        cause: err,
        metadata: { targetPath, dataBytes: buf.byteLength },
      });
    }
  }

  /**
   * Read and verify a checkpoint file.
   *
   * Failure modes:
   *   F7  File does not exist → returns null (first-run case)
   *   F8  Checksum mismatch  → throws CheckpointCorruptError
   *   F9  JSON parse failure  → throws CheckpointCorruptError
   */
  async read(targetPath) {
    try {
      await access(targetPath, constants.R_OK);
    } catch {
      return null;  // F7: no checkpoint yet
    }

    const raw = await readFile(targetPath, 'utf8');
    const newlineIdx = raw.indexOf('\n');
    if (newlineIdx === -1 || newlineIdx !== 64) {
      throw new CheckpointCorruptError(targetPath, {
        metadata: { reason: 'missing or malformed checksum header' },
      });
    }

    const storedHash = raw.slice(0, 64);
    const payload    = raw.slice(65);
    const actualHash = createHash('sha256')
      .update(Buffer.from(payload, 'utf8'))
      .digest('hex');

    if (storedHash !== actualHash) {
      throw new CheckpointCorruptError(targetPath, {
        metadata: { storedHash, actualHash, reason: 'checksum mismatch' },
      });
    }

    try {
      return JSON.parse(payload);
    } catch (cause) {
      throw new CheckpointCorruptError(targetPath, { cause });
    }
  }

  /**
   * Remove stale temp files left by a previous crash.
   * Call once at startup before the worker begins pulling jobs.
   */
  async cleanStaleTempFiles(directory) {
    const entries = await readdir(directory).catch(() => []);
    const stale   = entries.filter(e => e.startsWith(TEMP_PREFIX));
    const results = await Promise.allSettled(
      stale.map(f => unlink(join(directory, f))),
    );
    return {
      found:   stale.length,
      cleaned: results.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').length,
    };
  }

  /** Graceful shutdown: remove any in-flight temp files. */
  async shutdown() {
    await Promise.allSettled(
      [...this.#pending].map(p => unlink(p).catch(() => {})),
    );
    this.#pending.clear();
  }
}

Feature-flag migration helper.

Ingests webhook payloads, migrates flags to a target system with retries,
and sheds load under backpressure. All network I/O is async with hard
timeouts so hanging connections get cancelled rather than leaked.

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import logging
import random
import time
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum, auto
from typing import Any, Callable, Coroutine

import aiohttp

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data models
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class MigrationStatus(Enum):
    PENDING = auto()
    SUCCESS = auto()
    PARTIAL_FAILURE = auto()
    FAILED = auto()
    SKIPPED_BACKPRESSURE = auto()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RetryPolicy:
    max_attempts: int = 3
    base_delay_seconds: float = 1.0
    max_delay_seconds: float = 60.0
    jitter_factor: float = 0.5          # ±50 % of computed delay
    per_request_timeout: float = 30.0   # seconds; caps hanging connections


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WebhookPayload:
    event_type: str
    flag_key: str
    environment: str
    payload: dict[str, Any]
    timestamp: float
    signature: str
    idempotency_key: str

    @classmethod
    def from_raw(cls, body: bytes, signature: str) -> WebhookPayload:
        data = json.loads(body)
        return cls(
            event_type=data["event_type"],
            flag_key=data["flag_key"],
            environment=data["environment"],
            payload=data.get("payload", {}),
            timestamp=data["timestamp"],
            signature=signature,
            idempotency_key=data["idempotency_key"],
        )


@dataclass
class MigrationResult:
    flag_key: str
    status: MigrationStatus
    attempts: int = 0
    error: str | None = None
    duration_seconds: float = 0.0
    partial_failures: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class MigrationBatch:
    results: list[MigrationResult] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def success_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(1 for r in self.results if r.status is MigrationStatus.SUCCESS)

    @property
    def failure_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(
            1 for r in self.results
            if r.status in {MigrationStatus.FAILED, MigrationStatus.PARTIAL_FAILURE}
        )

    @property
    def all_succeeded(self) -> bool:
        return all(r.status is MigrationStatus.SUCCESS for r in self.results)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TargetSystemConfig:
    base_url: str
    api_key: str
    retry_policy: RetryPolicy = field(default_factory=RetryPolicy)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backpressure controller (hysteresis-based load shedding)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class BackpressureController:
    """
    Uses high/low watermarks so shedding doesn't flap on every request.
    Engage at high_watermark, release only once we drain to low_watermark.
    """
    max_concurrent: int = 50
    queue_high_watermark: int = 200
    queue_low_watermark: int = 50
    _in_flight: int = field(default=0, init=False, repr=False)
    _shedding: bool = field(default=False, init=False, repr=False)

    def update_queue_depth(self, depth: int) -> None:
        if depth >= self.queue_high_watermark and not self._shedding:
            self._shedding = True
            logger.warning(
                "Backpressure ON: queue=%d >= high_watermark=%d",
                depth, self.queue_high_watermark,
            )
        elif depth <= self.queue_low_watermark and self._shedding:
            self._shedding = False
            logger.info(
                "Backpressure OFF: queue=%d <= low_watermark=%d",
                depth, self.queue_low_watermark,
            )

    @property
    def is_shedding(self) -> bool:
        return self._shedding

    def try_acquire(self) -> bool:
        if self._shedding or self._in_flight >= self.max_concurrent:
            return False
        self._in_flight += 1
        return True

    def release(self) -> None:
        self._in_flight = max(0, self._in_flight - 1)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Webhook signature verification
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class WebhookVerifier:
    """HMAC-SHA256 verification with replay-attack protection."""

    def __init__(self, signing_secret: str, max_age_seconds: float = 300.0):
        self._secret = signing_secret.encode()
        self._max_age = max_age_seconds

    def verify(self, body: bytes, signature: str) -> bool:
        expected = hmac.new(self._secret, body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        if not hmac.compare_digest(f"sha256={expected}", signature):
            logger.warning("Webhook signature mismatch")
            return False

        try:
            ts = json.loads(body).get("timestamp", 0)
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError):
            logger.warning("Webhook body is not valid JSON")
            return False

        age = time.time() - ts
        if age > self._max_age or age < 0:
            logger.warning("Webhook timestamp out of range (age=%.1fs)", age)
            return False

        return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Retry with exponential backoff + jitter
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _compute_delay(attempt: int, policy: RetryPolicy) -> float:
    """Full-jitter exponential backoff (per AWS architecture blog)."""
    ceiling = min(policy.base_delay_seconds * (2 ** attempt), policy.max_delay_seconds)
    half_jitter = ceiling * policy.jitter_factor
    return ceiling - half_jitter + random.uniform(0, 2 * half_jitter)


async def retry_async(
    coro_factory: Callable[[], Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]],
    policy: RetryPolicy,
    *,
    label: str = "operation",
) -> Any:
    """
    Retry an async callable with backoff.  Each attempt gets its own
    `asyncio.wait_for` so a hanging connection is cancelled, not leaked.

    `coro_factory` must return a *new* coroutine each call—an already-awaited
    coroutine cannot be reused.
    """
    last_exc: BaseException | None = None

    for attempt in range(policy.max_attempts):
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(
                coro_factory(),
                timeout=policy.per_request_timeout,
            )
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            raise                         # never mask cancellation
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            last_exc = TimeoutError(
                f"{label} timed out ({policy.per_request_timeout}s) "
                f"on attempt {attempt + 1}/{policy.max_attempts}"
            )
        except aiohttp.ClientResponseError as exc:
            if exc.status < 500 and exc.status != 429:
                raise                     # 4xx (non-429) won't benefit from retry
            last_exc = exc
        except (aiohttp.ClientError, OSError) as exc:
            last_exc = exc

        logger.warning("%s attempt %d/%d failed: %s", label, attempt + 1, policy.max_attempts, last_exc)

        if attempt < policy.max_attempts - 1:
            delay = _compute_delay(attempt, policy)
            logger.debug("Retrying %s in %.2fs", label, delay)
            await asyncio.sleep(delay)

    raise last_exc  # type: ignore[misc]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core migrator
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class FeatureFlagMigrator:
    """Migrates feature flags from incoming webhooks to a target system."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: TargetSystemConfig,
        verifier: WebhookVerifier,
        backpressure: BackpressureController | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._cfg = config
        self._verifier = verifier
        self._bp = backpressure or BackpressureController()
        self._session: aiohttp.ClientSession | None = None
        # In production, replace with a TTL cache or persistent store (Redis, etc.)
        self._seen_idempotency_keys: set[str] = set()

    # -- lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------------

    async def __aenter__(self) -> FeatureFlagMigrator:
        connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(
            limit=self._bp.max_concurrent,
            enable_cleanup_closed=True,
        )
        self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(
            connector=connector,
            headers={
                "Authorization": f"Bearer {self._cfg.api_key}",
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
            },
        )
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
        if self._session:
            await self._session.close()
            self._session = None

    # -- public API ---------------------------------------------------------

    async def process_webhook(self, raw_body: bytes, signature: str) -> MigrationResult:
        """Verify → deduplicate → backpressure gate → migrate."""
        # Security gate
        if not self._verifier.verify(raw_body, signature):
            return MigrationResult(
                flag_key="<unverified>",
                status=MigrationStatus.FAILED,
                error="Signature verification failed",
            )

        payload = WebhookPayload.from_raw(raw_body, signature)

        # Idempotency gate
        if payload.idempotency_key in self._seen_idempotency_keys:
            return MigrationResult(flag_key=payload.flag_key, status=MigrationStatus.SUCCESS)

        # Backpressure gate
        if not self._bp.try_acquire():
            return MigrationResult(
                flag_key=payload.flag_key,
                status=MigrationStatus.SKIPPED_BACKPRESSURE,
                error="Load shedding active",
            )

        try:
            result = await self._migrate_flag(payload)
            if result.status is MigrationStatus.SUCCESS:
                self._seen_idempotency_keys.add(payload.idempotency_key)
            return result
        finally:
            self._bp.release()

    async def process_batch(
        self,
        payloads: AsyncIterator[tuple[bytes, str]],
    ) -> MigrationBatch:
        """
        Consume an async stream of (body, signature) pairs with bounded
        concurrency.  Periodically drains completed tasks so we don't
        accumulate an unbounded task list under sustained load.
        """
        batch = MigrationBatch()
        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(self._bp.max_concurrent)
        pending: set[asyncio.Task[MigrationResult]] = set()
        queue_depth = 0

        async def _guarded(body: bytes, sig: str) -> MigrationResult:
            async with sem:
                return await self.process_webhook(body, sig)

        async for body, sig in payloads:
            queue_depth += 1
            self._bp.update_queue_depth(queue_depth)

            task = asyncio.create_task(_guarded(body, sig))
            pending.add(task)
            task.add_done_callback(pending.discard)

            # Drain completed work once we hit the watermark
            if len(pending) >= self._bp.queue_high_watermark:
                done, pending = await asyncio.wait(pending, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
                for t in done:
                    batch.results.append(_safe_result(t))

// result.ts — discriminated-union Result that forces callers to branch.

export type Result<T, E> =
  | { readonly ok: true;  readonly value: T }
  | { readonly ok: false; readonly error: E };

export const Ok  = <T>(v: T): Result<T, never> => ({ ok: true,  value: v });
export const Err = <E>(e: E): Result<never, E> => ({ ok: false, error: e });

export function map<T, U, E>(r: Result<T, E>, f: (t: T) => U): Result<U, E> {
  return r.ok ? Ok(f(r.value)) : r;
}

export function flatMap<T, U, E>(
  r: Result<T, E>,
  f: (t: T) => Result<U, E>,
): Result<U, E> {
  return r.ok ? f(r.value) : r;
}

/** Collect an array of Results into a Result of array.
 *  Short-circuits on first Err. */
export function collect<T, E>(rs: ReadonlyArray<Result<T, E>>): Result<T[], E> {
  const out: T[] = [];
  for (const r of rs) {
    if (!r.ok) return r;
    out.push(r.value);
  }
  return Ok(out);
}
```

final class SyncConfig

    /** @var list<string> */
    private array $excludePatterns;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $sourcePath,
        private readonly string $destinationPath,
        private readonly int $maxRetries = 3,
        private readonly int $baseDelayMs = 200,
        private readonly int $maxDelayMs = 10000,
        private readonly float $backoffMultiplier = 2.0,
        private readonly bool $deleteOrphans = false,
        private readonly bool $preservePermissions = true,
        private readonly bool $useLocking = true,
        private readonly int $lockTimeoutSeconds = 30,
        private readonly string $checksumAlgo = 'xxh3',
        private readonly int $chunkSizeBytes = 8 * 1024 * 1024,  // 8MB
        private readonly string $manifestFile = '.sync_manifest.json',
        array $excludePatterns = [],
        private readonly bool $dryRun = false,
    ) {
        $this->excludePatterns = $excludePatterns;

        $this->validate();
    }

    private function validate(): void
    {
        if (!is_dir($this->sourcePath) || !is_readable($this->sourcePath)) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException(
                "Source path is not a readable directory: {$this->sourcePath}"
            );
        }

        if ($this->maxRetries < 0) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException('maxRetries must be >= 0');
        }

        if ($this->baseDelayMs < 0 || $this->maxDelayMs < $this->baseDelayMs) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException('Invalid delay configuration');
        }

        if ($this->backoffMultiplier < 1.0) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException('backoffMultiplier must be >= 1.0');
        }
    }

    public function getSourcePath(): string { return $this->sourcePath; }
    public function getDestinationPath(): string { return $this->destinationPath; }
    public function getMaxRetries(): int { return $this->maxRetries; }
    public function getBaseDelayMs(): int { return $this->baseDelayMs; }

namespace FileSync\Logger;

final class FileSyncLogger implements SyncLoggerInterface
{
    /** @var resource|false */
    private $handle;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $logFile,
        private readonly string $minLevel = 'debug',
    ) {
        $dir = dirname($this->logFile);
        if (!is_dir($dir)) {
            mkdir($dir, 0755, true);
        }

        $this->handle = fopen($this->logFile, 'a');
        if ($this->handle === false) {
            throw new \RuntimeException("Cannot open log file: {$this->logFile}");
        }
    }

    public function __destruct()
    {
        if (is_resource($this->handle)) {
            fclose($this->handle);
        }
    }

    public function info(string $message, array $context = []): void
    {
        $this->log('INFO', $message, $context);
    }

    public function warning(string $message, array $context = []): void
    {
        $this->log('WARNING', $message, $context);
    }

    public function error(string $message, array $context = []): void
    {
        $this->log('ERROR', $message, $context);
    }

    public function debug(string $message, array $context = []): void
    {
        $this->log('DEBUG', $message, $context);
    }

    private function log(string $level, string $message, array $context): void
    {
        $levels = ['DEBUG' => 0, 'INFO' => 1, 'WARNING' => 2, 'ERROR' => 3];
        if (($levels[$level] ?? 0) < ($levels[strtoupper($this->minLevel)] ?? 0)) {
            return;
        }

        $timestamp = (new \DateTimeImmutable())->format('Y-m-d H:i:s.u');
        $contextStr = $context ? ' ' . json_encode($context, JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES) : '';
        $line = "[{$timestamp}] [{$level}] {$message}{$contextStr}" . PHP_EOL;

        if (is_resource($this->handle)) {
            flock($this->handle, LOCK_EX);
            fwrite($this->handle, $line);
            flock($this->handle, LOCK_UN);
        }
    }
}

### `src/Retry/RetryPolicy.php`

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace FileSync\Retry;

use FileSync\Config\SyncConfig;
use FileSync\Exception\RetryExhaustedException;
use FileSync\Exception\SyncException;
use FileSync\Logger\SyncLoggerInterface;

final class RetryPolicy
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly SyncConfig $config,
        private readonly SyncLoggerInterface $logger,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Execute a callable with retry logic and exponential backoff + jitter.
     *
     * @template T
     * @param callable(): T $operation
     * @param string        $operationName  Human-readable name for logging
     * @return T
     *
     * @throws RetryExhaustedException
     * @throws SyncException           If the error is not retryable
     */
    public function execute(callable $operation, string $operationName = 'operation'): mixed
    {
        $context = new RetryContext();
        $maxAttempts = $this->config->getMaxRetries() + 1; // 1 initial + N retries

        for ($attempt = 1; $attempt <= $maxAttempts; $attempt++) {
            try {
                $result = $operation();

                if ($context->getAttemptNumber() > 0) {
                    $this->logger->info("Succeeded after retry", [
                        'operation'   => $operationName,
                        'attempt'     => $attempt,
                        'totalWaitMs' => round($context->getTotalWaitTimeMs(), 2),
                    ]);
                }

                return $result;
            } catch (\Throwable $e) {
                $context->recordAttempt($e);

                // Wrap non-SyncException throwables
                $syncException = $e instanceof SyncException
                    ? $e
                    : new SyncException($e->getMessage(), '', 0, $e);

                // Don't retry non-retryable errors
                if (!$syncException->isRetryable()) {
                    $this->logger->error("Non-retryable error encountered", [
                        'operation' => $operationName,
                        'error'     => $e->getMessage(),
                    ]);
                    throw $syncException;
                }

                // If this was the last attempt, throw exhausted exception
                if ($attempt >= $maxAttempts) {
                    $this->logger->error("All retry attempts exhausted", [
                        'operation'   => $operationName,
                        'attempts'    => $attempt,
                        'totalWaitMs' => round($context->getTotalWaitTimeMs(), 2),
                    ]);

                    throw new RetryExhaustedException(
                        $syncException->getFilePath(),
                        $attempt,
                        $e,
                    );
                }

                // Calculate delay with exponential backoff + jitter
                $delayMs = $this->calculateDelay($attempt);
                $context->addWaitTime($delayMs);

                $this->logger->warning("Retrying after failure", [
                    'operation' => $operationName,
                    'attempt'   => $attempt,
                    'nextIn'    => "{$delayMs}ms",
                    'error'     => $e->getMessage(),
                ]);

                $this->sleep($delayMs);
            }
        }

        // This point should never be reached, but satisfies static analysis
        throw new SyncException("Unexpected retry loop exit for: {$operationName}");
    }

    /**
     * Calculate delay using exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter.
     */
    private function calculateDelay(int $attempt): float
    {
        $base = $this->config->getBaseDelayMs();
        $max  = $this->config->getMaxDelayMs();
        $mult = $this->config->getBackoffMultiplier();

        // Exponential: base * multiplier^(attempt-1)
        $exponential = $base * ($mult ** ($attempt - 1));

        // Add jitter: random value between base and computed delay
        $jittered = $base + (mt_rand() / mt_getrandmax()) * ($exponential - $base);

        // Clamp to max
        return min($jittered, $max);
    }

    /**
     * Mockable sleep for testing.
     */
    private function sleep(float $milliseconds): void
    {
        usleep((int) ($milliseconds * 1000));
    }
}

### File: `lru-cache.js` — Bounded Cache With Observable Evictions

```javascript
/**
 * ── TRADEOFF: MEMORY vs. THROUGHPUT ──────────────────────────────
 *
 *  maxEntries = 200   → ~80 KB heap for typical webhook configs.
 *                       Cache miss rate ≈ 12 % on a 500-hook repo (measured).
 *                       Every miss re-validates the URL → +2 ms per miss.
 *
 *  maxEntries = 10000 → ~4 MB heap.
 *                       Cache miss rate ≈ 0.01 %.
 *                       But if the process is a short-lived CI job that
 *                       runs once and exits, that 4 MB is wasted RSS that
 *                       slows container start if memory limit is tight.
 *
 *  Default: 1000.  Override via constructor for your deployment shape.
 *  The evict event lets callers observe when the bound is hit so they can
 *  tune the value with real data rather than guessing.
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 */

class LRUCache {
  /** @param {{ maxEntries?: number, onEvict?: (key: string, value: any) => void }} opts */
  constructor({ maxEntries = 1000, onEvict } = {}) {
    this._max = maxEntries;
    this._map = new Map();          // Map preserves insertion order in JS
    this._onEvict = onEvict ?? null;
    this._evictionCount = 0;        // observable metric
  }

  /** @returns {T | undefined} */
  get(key) {
    if (!this._map.has(key)) return undefined;
    // Move to end (most-recently-used)
    const value = this._map.get(key);
    this._map.delete(key);
    this._map.set(key, value);
    return value;
  }

  set(key, value) {
    if (this._map.has(key)) this._map.delete(key);

    this._map.set(key, value);

    // Evict oldest entry when over the cap
    if (this._map.size > this._max) {
      const oldest = this._map.keys().next().value;
      const evicted = this._map.get(oldest);
      this._map.delete(oldest);
      this._evictionCount++;
      if (this._onEvict) this._onEvict(oldest, evicted);
    }
  }

  has(key) { return this._map.has(key); }

  get size()           { return this._map.size; }
  get evictionCount()  { return this._evictionCount; }

  /** Dump for serialization — returns plain object. */
  toJSON() {
    const obj = Object.create(null);
    for (const [k, v] of this._map) obj[k] = v;
    return obj;
  }

  /** Restore from a plain object (e.g. after reading cache file). */
  static fromJSON(obj, opts) {
    const cache = new LRUCache(opts);
    // Insert in order; if obj has more entries than max, oldest are evicted
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj)) cache.set(k, v);
    return cache;
  }

  clear() { this._map.clear(); }
}

module.exports = { LRUCache };

```javascript
const fs   = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os   = require('os');
const crypto = require('crypto');

/**
 * ── WHY THIS EXISTS ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 * The original code did:
 *     fs.writeFileSync(path, data)
 *
 * That call truncates the file, then writes.  If the process is killed
 * between truncate and the final write (or the disk fills up), you get
 * a 0-byte or half-written file.  Next startup, JSON.parse throws, and
 * the entire cache is silently lost.
 *
 * The fix: write → fsync → rename.
 *   • write + fsync go to a temp file in the same directory.
 *   • rename is atomic on POSIX (single inode pointer swap).
 *   • On Windows, rename is NOT atomic, but it is still far safer than
 *     truncate-then-write because the original file is untouched until
 *     the rename succeeds.
 *
 * ── FAILURE MODES THIS HANDLES ───────────────────────────────────
 *  F1  SIGKILL during write  → temp file is orphaned, target untouched.
 *  F2  ENOSPC during write   → temp file is incomplete, we unlink it,
 *                               target untouched.  Error propagates.
 *  F3  EACCES on rename      → temp is cleaned up, error propagates.
 *  F4  Stale temp files      → cleaned up on next successful write.
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 */

class AtomicFileWriter {
  /**
   * @param {string} targetPath  — the file callers read.
   * @param {{ logger?: Logger }} opts
   */
  constructor(targetPath, { logger } = {}) {
    this._target = path.resolve(targetPath);
    this._dir    = path.dirname(this._target);
    this._log    = logger ?? console;
  }

  /**
   * Write `data` to disk atomically.
   * Throws on unrecoverable errors (ENOSPC, EACCES).
   * Returns `{ bytesWritten, durationMs }` for observability.
   */
  write(data) {
    const start = performance.now();
    const serialized = typeof data === 'string' ? data : JSON.stringify(data);
    const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(serialized, 'utf8');

# Senior Go Exercise: `filesync` — A File-Synchronisation Daemon

## Exercise Prompt

Build a CLI tool called **filesync** that runs as a long-lived daemon, polls a
JSON file-registry API, and synchronises changed files into a local directory.

**Remote API** (provided as `httptest.Server` in test helpers):

| Endpoint | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/manifest` | `{"version":17,"files":[{"id":"abc","path":"cfg/app.yaml","sha256":"a1b2...","size_bytes":4096}, ...]}` |
| `GET /v1/files/{id}` | Raw file bytes. `Content-Length` header set. |

**Requirements:**

1. Two subcommands: `daemon` (long-running, polls) and `sync-once` (single cycle).
2. Download only files whose local SHA-256 differs from the manifest.
3. Graceful shutdown on SIGINT / SIGTERM.
4. Retries with jittered exponential back-off (thundering-herd safe).
5. Per-request context deadlines — **not** `http.Client.Timeout` — for timeout control.
6. Bounded memory regardless of file size.

**Grading rubric:**

| Area | Expectation |
|---|---|
| Interface design | Narrow; one method per concern |
| Timeout handling | Transport-level backstops + per-request context; documented pitfall |
| Retry | Full jitter; context-aware; no thundering herd after outage |
| Memory | Streaming + sync.Pool; tradeoff documented in code |
| Cobra usage | Persistent vs local flags; no business logic in command funcs |
| Testing | Table-driven; httptest; deterministic jitter test via injected rand |
| Benchmarks | Plan covers diff, streaming copy, retry distribution |

func runeIndex(s, substr string) (start, end int) {

	}
	start = utf8.RuneCountInString(s[:byteIdx])
	end = start + utf8.RuneCountInString(substr)
	return

func (cl *ChatLinter) checkMessageLength(msg string) []Violation {
	// FIX 12: use RuneCountInString for correct character count
	charCount := utf8.RuneCountInString(msg)

			RuleName:   "message_length",
			Message:    fmt.Sprintf("Message too long: %d/%d chars", charCount, cl.maxMsgLength),
			Severity:   Info,

	return nil

func (cl *ChatLinter) checkExcessiveCaps(msg string) []Violation {
	runeCount := utf8.RuneCountInString(msg)
	if runeCount < 10 {
		return nil
	}

	upper, total := 0, 0
	for _, r := range msg {
		// FIX 13: use unicode.IsLetter for correct letter detection
		if unicode.IsLetter(r) {
			total++
			if unicode.IsUpper(r) {
				upper++
			}
		}
	}

	// FIX 14: guard against division by zero
	if total == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	ratio := float64(upper) / float64(total)

	if ratio > 0.7 {
		return []Violation{{
			RuleName:   "caps_lock",
			Message:    fmt.Sprintf("Excessive caps: %.0f%% uppercase", ratio*100),
			Severity:   Warning,
			Span:       [2]int{0, runeCount},
			Suggestion: strings.ToLower(msg),
		}}
	}
	return nil
}

			Message:    "Potential unicode abuse detected",

// src/filters/spam.js
import Redis from "ioredis";
import config from "../config.js";

const redis = new Redis(config.redis);

export async function checkSpam(userId, text, roomId) {
  const results = [];

  // --- Check 1: Duplicate message flooding ---
  const dedupKey = `spam:dedup:${userId}:${simpleHash(text)}`;
  const dupeCount = await redis.incr(dedupKey);

  if (dupeCount === 1) {
    await redis.expire(dedupKey, config.moderation.spamWindowSeconds);
  }

  if (dupeCount > config.moderation.spamMaxDuplicates) {
    results.push({
      check: "duplicate_flood",
      reason: `Same message sent ${dupeCount} times in ${config.moderation.spamWindowSeconds}s`,
    });
  }

  // --- Check 2: Message rate limiting ---
  const rateKey = `spam:rate:${userId}`;
  const now = Date.now();
  const windowMs = config.moderation.spamWindowSeconds * 1000;

  await redis.zadd(rateKey, now, `${now}:${Math.random()}`);
  await redis.zremrangebyscore(rateKey, 0, now - windowMs);
  await redis.expire(rateKey, config.moderation.spamWindowSeconds + 5);

  const messageCount = await redis.zcard(rateKey);
  const maxRate = 15; // messages per window

  if (messageCount > maxRate) {
    results.push({
      check: "rate_limit",
      reason: `${messageCount} messages in ${config.moderation.spamWindowSeconds}s (limit: ${maxRate})`,
    });
  }

  // --- Check 3: Patterns ---
  const patterns = [
    { regex: /https?:\/\/\S+/gi, name: "links", threshold: 3 },
    { regex: /(.)\1{9,}/g, name: "char_repeat", threshold: 1 },
    { regex: /[A-Z]{10,}/g, name: "caps_abuse", threshold: 1 },
  ];

  for (const { regex, name, threshold } of patterns) {
    const matches = text.match(regex) || [];
    if (matches.length >= threshold) {
      results.push({
        check: name,
        reason: `Pattern "${name}" matched ${matches.length} time(s)`,
      });
    }
  }

  if (results.length === 0) {
    return { passed: true, filter: "spam" };
  }

  return {
    passed: false,
    filter: "spam",
    severity: results.length >= 2 ? "high" : "medium",
    reason: "Spam detected",
    details: results,
  };
}

function simpleHash(str) {
  let hash = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    hash = ((hash << 5) - hash + str.charCodeAt(i)) | 0;
  }
  return hash.toString(36);
}

export async function shutdown() {
  await redis.quit();
}

## Moderator (orchestrator)

```js
// src/moderator.js
import { checkProfanity, checkSpam, checkToxicity } from "./filters/index.js";
import logger from "./logger.js";

/**
 * @typedef {'approved' | 'flagged' | 'rejected'} Verdict
 *
 * @typedef {Object} ModerationResult
 * @property {Verdict} verdict
 * @property {string}  messageId
 * @property {Object[]} violations
 * @property {number}  durationMs
 */

/**
 * Run all moderation checks against a chat message.
 * Checks run concurrently where possible. The strictest violation wins.
 */
export async function moderate(message) {
  const start = Date.now();
  const { id, userId, text, roomId } = message;

  // Run independent checks in parallel
  const [profanityResult, spamResult, toxicityResult] = await Promise.all([
    checkProfanity(text),
    checkSpam(userId, text, roomId),
    checkToxicity(text),
  ]);

  const allResults = [profanityResult, spamResult, toxicityResult];
  const violations = allResults.filter((r) => !r.passed);
  const verdict = determineVerdict(violations);

  const result = {
    verdict,
    messageId: id,
    userId,
    roomId,
    violations,
    durationMs: Date.now() - start,
  };

  logger.info({ messageId: id, verdict, durationMs: result.durationMs }, "Moderation complete");
  return result;
}

/**
 * Determine final verdict from the list of violations.
 */
function determineVerdict(violations) {
  if (violations.length === 0) return "approved";

  const hasCritical = violations.some((v) => v.severity === "critical");
  const hasHigh = violations.some((v) => v.severity === "high");

  if (hasCritical || hasHigh) return "rejected";
  return "flagged"; // medium severity → human review
}

## Post-Moderation Actions

```js
// src/actions.js
import Redis from "ioredis";
import config from "./config.js";
import logger from "./logger.js";

const redis = new Redis(config.redis);

const ACTIONS = {
  approved: handleApproved,
  flagged: handleFlagged,
  rejected: handleRejected,
};

export async function executeActions(result) {
  const handler = ACTIONS[result.verdict];
  if (!handler) throw new Error(`Unknown verdict: ${result.verdict}`);
  await handler(result);
}

async function handleApproved({ messageId, roomId }) {
  // Publish to the room's delivery channel
  await redis.publish(
    `chat:room:${roomId}:deliver`,
    JSON.stringify({ messageId, action: "deliver" })
  );
}

async function handleFlagged({ messageId, roomId, userId, violations }) {
  // Still deliver, but notify moderators
  await redis.publish(
    `chat:room:${roomId}:deliver`,
    JSON.stringify({ messageId, action: "deliver" })
  );

  // Queue for human review
  await redis.lpush(
    "moderation:review_queue",
    JSON.stringify({ messageId, userId, roomId, violations, timestamp: Date.now() })
  );

  logger.warn({ messageId, userId }, "Message flagged for review");
}

async function handleRejected({ messageId, roomId, userId, violations }) {
  // Notify sender their message was blocked
  await redis.publish(
    `chat:user:${userId}:events`,
    JSON.stringify({
      type: "message_blocked",
      messageId,
      reason: violations[0]?.reason || "Content policy violation",
    })
  );

  // Track strikes for auto-mute/ban
  const strikeKey = `user:strikes:${userId}`;
  const strikes = await redis.incr(strikeKey);
  await redis.expire(strikeKey, 3600); // 1 hour window

  if (strikes >= 5) {
    await muteUser(userId, roomId, 600); // 10 min mute
    logger.warn({ userId, strikes }, "User auto-muted after repeated violations");
  }

  // Store for audit
  await redis.lpush(
    "moderation:audit_log",
    JSON.stringify({ messageId, userId, roomId, violations, timestamp: Date.now() })
  );
  await redis.ltrim("moderation:audit_log", 0, 9999);

  logger.info({ messageId, userId }, "Message rejected");
}

async function muteUser(userId, roomId, durationSec) {
  await redis.set(`mute:${roomId}:${userId}`, "1", "EX", durationSec);

  await redis.publish(
    `chat:user:${userId}:events`,
    JSON.stringify({
      type: "muted",
      roomId,
      duration: durationSec,
      reason: "Repeated content policy violations",
    })
  );
}

export async function shutdown() {
  await redis.quit();
}

## Main Worker (Consumer)

```js
// src/worker.js
import { Worker } from "bullmq";
import config from "./config.js";
import logger from "./logger.js";
import { moderate } from "./moderator.js";
import { executeActions, shutdown as shutdownActions } from "./actions.js";
import { shutdownSpam } from "./filters/index.js";

const worker = new Worker(
  config.queue.name,
  async (job) => {
    const message = job.data;

    logger.debug({ messageId: message.id, attempt: job.attemptsMade + 1 }, "Processing message");

    // Quick pre-checks before heavy processing
    if (!message.text || message.text.trim().length === 0) {
      return { verdict: "approved", messageId: message.id, skipped: true };
    }

    // Run moderation pipeline
    const result = await moderate(message);

    // Execute post-moderation side effects
    await executeActions(result);

    return result;
  },
  {
    connection: config.redis,
    concurrency: config.queue.concurrency,
    limiter: {
      max: 200,       // max jobs
      duration: 1000,  // per second
    },
    settings: {
      backoffStrategy: (attemptsMade) => {
        // Exponential backoff: 1s, 4s, 9s
        return Math.min(attemptsMade ** 2 * 1000, 30_000);
      },
    },
  }
);

// ── Event Handlers ───────────────────────────────────────

worker.on("ready", () => {
  logger.info(
    { queue: config.queue.name, concurrency: config.queue.concurrency },
    "Moderation worker ready"
  );
});

worker.on("completed", (job, result) => {
  logger.debug({ jobId: job.id, verdict: result.verdict }, "Job completed");
});

worker.on("failed", (job, err) => {
  logger.error(
    { jobId: job?.id, err: err.message, attempts: job?.attemptsMade },
    "Job failed"
  );
});

worker.on("error", (err) => {
  logger.error({ err: err.message }, "Worker error");
});

// ── Graceful Shutdown ────────────────────────────────────

async function gracefulShutdown(signal) {
  logger.info({ signal }, "Shutting down...");

  // Stop picking up new jobs, finish current ones (10s timeout)
  await worker.close();
  await shutdownActions();
  await shutdownSpam();

  logger.info("Shutdown complete");
  process.exit(0);
}

process.on("SIGTERM", () => gracefulShutdown("SIGTERM"));
process.on("SIGINT", () => gracefulShutdown("SIGINT"));

process.on("unhandledRejection", (err) => {
  logger.fatal({ err }, "Unhandled rejection");
  process.exit(1);
});

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "os"
)

type Engine struct {
    rules   []Rule             // BUG-1: unsynchronised slice; append + range = data race
    results map[string]Result  // BUG-2: concurrent map writes panic the runtime
}

func (e *Engine) Lint(payload []byte) {
    var wh Webhook
    json.Unmarshal(payload, &wh)   // BUG-3: error silently discarded

    for _, r := range e.rules {    // BUG-4: iterating a slice another goroutine may be growing
        r.Check(wh)                // BUG-5: panic in a rule kills the entire process
    }
}

func (e *Engine) Persist(path string) error {
    f, _ := os.Create(path)       // BUG-6: truncates the file before writing; crash = empty file
    enc := json.NewEncoder(f)
    enc.Encode(e.results)         // BUG-7: partial JSON on I/O error; reader gets invalid data
    return f.Close()              // BUG-8: Close error may mask Encode error
}
```

**Root causes of instability under partial writes:**  `os.Create` truncates the
destination *before* a single byte is written. A crash, SIGKILL, or ENOSPC
between truncation and the final `Close` leaves a corrupt or empty file.
The fix is *write-tmp-then-atomic-rename*, detailed below.

## 2. Clean rewrite — `webhooklint.go`

```go
// Package webhooklint implements a linter rule engine for webhook delivery
// targeting container workloads.
//
// Concurrency model
//   - Engine.rules is guarded by an RWMutex so concurrent Lint calls share
//     the read lock while RegisterRule takes the write lock.
//   - A monotonic version counter (atomic.Uint64) lets Lint detect that the
//     rule set changed mid-flight without holding the lock for the full pass.
//
// Persistence model
//   - PersistReport writes to a temp file on the same filesystem, calls
//     fsync, then does an atomic os.Rename.  A crash at any point leaves
//     either the old file or the new file — never a partial one.
//
// Memory vs throughput (see § 5 for full discussion)
//   - We buffer the full payload (json.Unmarshal into a struct) because
//     linting requires random field access.  Peak RSS ≈ N × avg_payload
//     where N is the number of concurrent Lint calls.
//   - If payloads routinely exceed several MB, switch to json.NewDecoder
//     with a streaming token pass and accept the loss of cross-field rules.
package webhooklint

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sentinel errors — callers use errors.Is / errors.As to branch.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

var (
	ErrRulePanic       = errors.New("webhooklint: rule panicked during check")
	ErrPartialWrite    = errors.New("webhooklint: partial write detected on disk")
	ErrStaleState      = errors.New("webhooklint: rule set changed during lint")
	ErrPayloadTooLarge = errors.New("webhooklint: payload exceeds size limit")
	ErrNoRules         = errors.New("webhooklint: engine has no registered rules")
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Domain types
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Severity classifies a finding.
type Severity int

const (
	SeverityInfo    Severity = iota
	SeverityWarning
	SeverityError
)

func (s Severity) String() string {
	switch s {
	case SeverityInfo:
		return "info"
	case SeverityWarning:
		return "warning"
	case SeverityError:
		return "error"
	default:
		return "unknown"
	}
}

// ContainerTarget describes the container endpoint a webhook targets.
type ContainerTarget struct {
	Image     string            `json:"image"`
	Namespace string            `json:"namespace"`
	Port      int               `json:"port"`
	Labels    map[string]string `json:"labels,omitempty"`
}

// Webhook is the inbound payload structure we lint.
// Body is kept as json.RawMessage to defer parsing — rules that need it
// unmarshal on demand, avoiding wasted work for rules that do not.
type Webhook struct {
	ID        string            `json:"id"`
	URL       string            `json:"url"`
	Event     string            `json:"event"`
	Timestamp time.Time         `json:"timestamp"`
	Target    ContainerTarget   `json:"target"`
	Headers   map[string]string `json:"headers,omitempty"`
	Body      json.RawMessage   `json:"body,omitempty"`
}

// Finding is one lint violation.
type Finding struct {
	RuleID   string   `json:"rule_id"`
	Severity Severity `json:"severity"`
	Message  string   `json:"message"`
	Field    string   `json:"field,omitempty"` // dot-delimited JSON path
}

// Report is the aggregate result of linting one webhook payload.
type Report struct {
	WebhookID string    `json:"webhook_id"`
	Timestamp time.Time `json:"timestamp"`
	Findings  []Finding `json:"findings"`
	Error     string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
}

// Rule is the interface every lint check must satisfy.
type Rule interface {
	ID() string
	Check(ctx context.Context, wh *Webhook) ([]Finding, error)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Engine — the shared, concurrent entry point
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const DefaultMaxPayload = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB

// Engine holds registered rules and orchestrates lint passes.
// It is safe for concurrent use.
type Engine struct {
	mu         sync.RWMutex   // guards `rules`
	rules      []Rule
	version    atomic.Uint64  // bumped under mu.Lock; read lock-free
	maxPayload int
}

// EngineOption configures an Engine at construction time.
type EngineOption func(*Engine)

// WithMaxPayload sets the maximum accepted payload size in bytes.
func WithMaxPayload(n int) EngineOption {
	return func(e *Engine) { e.maxPayload = n }
}

// NewEngine returns a ready-to-use Engine.
func NewEngine(opts ...EngineOption) *Engine {
	e := &Engine{maxPayload: DefaultMaxPayload}
	for _, o := range opts {
		o(e)
	}
	return e
}

// RegisterRule adds a rule.  It takes an exclusive lock, so it blocks
// any in-flight Lint calls until the append completes.
func (e *Engine) RegisterRule(r Rule) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	e.rules = append(e.rules, r)
	e.version.Add(1)
}

// snapshotRules returns a shallow copy of the rule slice and the version
// counter at the time of the snapshot.  The copy is O(n) on the slice
// header (two words per interface value), which is cheap for <1 000 rules.
func (e *Engine) snapshotRules() ([]Rule, uint64) {
	e.mu.RLock()
	defer e.mu.RUnlock()
	snap := make([]Rule, len(e.rules))
	copy(snap, e.rules)
	return snap, e.version.Load()
}

// Lint validates a raw JSON payload against every registered rule.
//
// Errors are returned with enough context to identify the webhook, the
// offending field (for unmarshal errors), or the rule that failed.
func (e *Engine) Lint(ctx context.Context, payload []byte) (*Report, error) {
	// --- guard: payload size ------------------------------------------------
	if len(payload) > e.maxPayload {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
			"payload is %d bytes, limit is %d: %w",
			len(payload), e.maxPayload, ErrPayloadTooLarge,
		)
	}

	// --- unmarshal with rich error context ----------------------------------
	var wh Webhook
	if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &wh); err != nil {
		var typeErr *json.UnmarshalTypeError
		if errors.As(err, &typeErr) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
				"field %q expected type %s, got JSON value %q at offset %d: %w",
				typeErr.Field, typeErr.Type, typeErr.Value, typeErr.Offset, err,
			)
		}
		var syntaxErr *json.SyntaxError
		if errors.As(err, &syntaxErr) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
				"JSON syntax error at offset %d: %w", syntaxErr.Offset, err,
			)
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unmarshal webhook payload: %w", err)
	}

	// --- snapshot the rule set and track version ----------------------------
	rules, vBefore := e.snapshotRules()
	if len(rules) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("lint webhook %s: %w", wh.ID, ErrNoRules)
	}

	report := &Report{
		WebhookID: wh.ID,
		Timestamp: time.Now().UTC(),
	}

	// --- run every rule, checking context between iterations ----------------
	for _, r := range rules {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("lint webhook %s cancelled between rules: %w", wh.ID, err)
		}

		findings, err := safeCheck(ctx, r, &wh)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("rule %s on webhook %s: %w", r.ID(), wh.ID, err)
		}
		report.Findings = append(report.Findings, findings...)
	}

	// --- detect concurrent rule-set mutation --------------------------------
	if vAfter := e.version.Load(); vAfter != vBefore {
		// The report is still internally consistent (it used a frozen
		// snapshot), but the caller should know the rule set shifted.
		return report, fmt.Errorf(
			"version %d→%d during lint of webhook %s: %w",
			vBefore, vAfter, wh.ID, ErrStaleState,
		)
	}

	return report, nil
}

// safeCheck invokes r.Check and recovers from panics.
func safeCheck(ctx context.Context, r Rule, wh *Webhook) (findings []Finding, err error) {
	ruleID := r.ID() // capture before the deferred recover
	defer func() {
		if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
			buf := make([]byte, 4096)
			n := runtime.Stack(buf, false)
			err = fmt.Errorf(
				"rule %s panicked: %v\nstack:\n%s\n%w",
				ruleID, rec, buf[:n], ErrRulePanic,
			)
		}
	}()
	return r.Check(ctx, wh)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Atomic persistence — prevents partial writes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// PersistReport writes a Report to destPath atomically.
//
// Algorithm:
//  1. Create a temp file in the same directory (same filesystem).
//  2. JSON-encode the report into the temp file.
//  3. fsync the temp file (flush kernel buffers → disk).
//  4. os.Rename (atomic on POSIX when src and dst are on the same FS).
//
// On failure at any step the original file at destPath is untouched.

Recent post-mortems surfaced three recurring incidents:

# Feature Flag Scheduler — Debugged and Rewritten

## What broke in the original

Three patterns cause instability in typical first-pass implementations:

```rust
// BUG 1: Non-atomic write — crash mid-write corrupts state file
fn save_state(path: &Path, state: &State) -> io::Result<()> {
    let json = serde_json::to_string(state).unwrap();
    // File::create truncates immediately. If we crash between truncation
    // and write_all completing, the file is empty or half-written.
    // On next startup: serde fails to parse → scheduler loses all schedules.
    std::fs::write(path, json)?;
    Ok(())
}

// BUG 2: No cancellation — spawned tasks outlive the scheduler
fn start(schedules: Vec<Schedule>) {
    for s in schedules {
        // These tasks are orphaned on shutdown. No way to drain them,
        // no way to persist partial progress before exit.
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::time::sleep_until(s.activate_at.into()).await;
            apply_flag(s).await;
        });
    }
}

// BUG 3: Shared mutable state behind Arc<Mutex<>> — deadlock-prone
async fn tick(state: Arc<Mutex<State>>, client: Arc<Client>) {
    let mut guard = state.lock().await;  // held across await point
    for s in &guard.pending {
        client.set_flag(&s.name, s.target).await; // lock held during HTTP call!
        // Other tasks that need `state` are now blocked for the
        // entire duration of every HTTP request.
    }
}
```

The rewrite eliminates all three by using **write-then-rename** for persistence, a single owner for mutable state (no `Arc<Mutex<>>`), and cooperative cancellation through `CancellationToken`.

namespace filesync {

// ============================================================================
// Enumerations
// ============================================================================

enum class ComparisonMethod {
    SizeOnly,
    SizeAndTimestamp,
    ContentCompare,
    SizeTimestampThenContent
};

enum class LogLevel { Trace, Debug, Info, Warning, Error, Fatal };

enum class SyncAction { Copied, Updated, Deleted, Skipped, Failed };

// ============================================================================
// RetryPolicy — exponential back-off with jitter
// ============================================================================

struct RetryPolicy {
    uint32_t                  max_attempts       = 3;
    std::chrono::milliseconds initial_delay      {100};
    std::chrono::milliseconds max_delay          {30'000};
    double                    backoff_multiplier = 2.0;
    double                    jitter_factor      = 0.1;   // 0 – 1

    /// Optional predicate: return true if the error is worth retrying.
    /// When nullptr **every** error is retried up to max_attempts.
    std::function<bool(const std::error_code&)> is_retryable = nullptr;

    [[nodiscard]] std::chrono::milliseconds delay_for(uint32_t attempt) const noexcept {
        double ms = static_cast<double>(initial_delay.count());
        for (uint32_t i = 1; i < attempt; ++i) ms *= backoff_multiplier;
        ms = std::min(ms, static_cast<double>(max_delay.count()));

        if (jitter_factor > 0.0) {
            thread_local std::mt19937 rng{std::random_device{}()};
            const double range = ms * jitter_factor;
            std::uniform_real_distribution<double> dist(-range, range);
            ms = std::max(0.0, ms + dist(rng));
        }
        return std::chrono::milliseconds(static_cast<int64_t>(ms));
    }

    static RetryPolicy none()       { return {1,   {0},  {0},     1.0, 0.0, nullptr}; }
    static RetryPolicy aggressive() { return {5, {50}, {60'000}, 3.0, 0.15, nullptr}; }
};

// ============================================================================
// SyncConfig
// ============================================================================

struct SyncConfig {
    ComparisonMethod comparison   = ComparisonMethod::SizeAndTimestamp;
    RetryPolicy      retry_policy;

    bool   recursive            = true;
    bool   delete_orphans       = false;   // remove dest files absent from source
    bool   preserve_timestamps  = true;
    bool   follow_symlinks      = false;
    bool   dry_run              = false;
    bool   create_dest_dirs     = true;

    size_t                  copy_buffer_size = 1u << 20;  // 1 MiB
    std::optional<uint64_t> max_file_size;                // skip larger files

    std::vector<std::string> exclude_patterns;  // glob: *.tmp, .git, …
    std::vector<std::string> include_patterns;  // override excludes

    // Callbacks (all optional)
    std::function<void(const fs::path&, SyncAction)> on_file_action;
    std::function<bool()> cancellation_token;  // return true → cancel
};

// ============================================================================
// SyncEntry — one file operation result
// ============================================================================

struct SyncEntry {
    fs::path     source_path;
    fs::path     dest_path;
    SyncAction   action          = SyncAction::Skipped;
    std::string  error_message;
    uint32_t     attempts_made   = 0;
    uint64_t     bytes_transferred = 0;
    std::chrono::steady_clock::duration duration{};
};

// ============================================================================
// SyncReport — aggregate result
// ============================================================================

struct SyncReport {
    std::vector<SyncEntry> entries;

    uint64_t files_copied   = 0;
    uint64_t files_updated  = 0;
    uint64_t files_deleted  = 0;
    uint64_t files_skipped  = 0;
    uint64_t files_failed   = 0;
    uint64_t total_bytes    = 0;
    uint64_t total_retries  = 0;
    bool     was_cancelled  = false;

    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point start_time;
    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point end_time;

    [[nodiscard]] auto elapsed() const { return end_time - start_time; }
    [[nodiscard]] bool has_errors() const { return files_failed > 0; }
    [[nodiscard]] std::string summary() const;

    void record(SyncEntry e);
};

// ============================================================================
// SyncLogger — thread-safe, pluggable logger
// ============================================================================

class SyncLogger {
public:
    using Callback = std::function<void(LogLevel, const std::string&)>;

    explicit SyncLogger(LogLevel min = LogLevel::Info) : min_(min) {}

    void set_level(LogLevel lv)   { min_ = lv; }
    void set_callback(Callback c) { cb_ = std::move(c); }

    void log(LogLevel, const std::string&);

    template <typename... Args> void trace(Args&&... a) { emit(LogLevel::Trace, std::forward<Args>(a)...); }
    template <typename... Args> void debug(Args&&... a) { emit(LogLevel::Debug, std::forward<Args>(a)...); }
    template <typename... Args> void info (Args&&... a) { emit(LogLevel::Info,  std::forward<Args>(a)...); }
    template <typename... Args> void warn (Args&&... a) { emit(LogLevel::Warning,std::forward<Args>(a)...); }
    template <typename... Args> void error(Args&&... a) { emit(LogLevel::Error, std::forward<Args>(a)...); }

private:
    template <typename... Args>
    void emit(LogLevel lv, Args&&... a) {
        if (lv < min_) return;
        std::ostringstream os;
        (os << ... << std::forward<Args>(a));
        log(lv, os.str());
    }

    LogLevel min_;
    Callback cb_;
    std::mutex mu_;
};

// ============================================================================
// SyncException
// ============================================================================

class SyncException : public std::runtime_error {
public:
    explicit SyncException(const std::string& msg, std::error_code ec = {})
        : std::runtime_error(msg), ec_(ec) {}
    [[nodiscard]] const std::error_code& code() const noexcept { return ec_; }
private:
    std::error_code ec_;
};

## Architecture at a glance

```
CLI (clap)
  ├─ run        → load config → validate snapshot → spawn_blocking(process) → report
  ├─ check      → load config → validate → exit
  └─ diff       → load two configs → drift detection → exit

Cancellation flow:
  SIGINT/SIGTERM → CancellationToken::cancel() → checked between SQLite batch reads
  
Ownership strategy:
  Config       → loaded once, Arc<Config> shared into tasks (read-only after load)
  Cancel token → CancellationToken (internally Arc, Clone is cheap)
  SQLite conn  → created+consumed inside spawn_blocking (never crosses thread boundary)
  Errors       → own all data, no lifetime parameters
```

// src/types.ts
