/** Discriminated result — forces callers to handle the error branch. */
export type Result<T, E extends BaseError = BaseError> =
  | { readonly ok: true; readonly value: T }
  | { readonly ok: false; readonly error: E };

export function Ok<T>(value: T): Result<T, never> {
  return { ok: true, value };
}

export function Err<E extends BaseError>(error: E): Result<never, E> {
  return { ok: false, error };
}

/** Branded string so a raw string can't pass where an env name is needed. */
declare const ENV_BRAND: unique symbol;
export type EnvironmentName = string & { readonly [ENV_BRAND]: true };

export function toEnvironmentName(raw: string): EnvironmentName {
  // FAILURE MODE: empty or whitespace-only environment name
  //   surfaced as a thrown TypeError synchronously at startup.
  const trimmed = raw.trim();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) {
    throw new TypeError("Environment name must be non-empty");
  }
  return trimmed as EnvironmentName;
}

/** Opaque cents representation — prevents floating-point dollar math. */
declare const CENTS_BRAND: unique symbol;
export type CentsAmount = number & { readonly [CENTS_BRAND]: true };

export function toCents(dollars: number): CentsAmount {
  // FAILURE MODE: NaN or Infinity propagation from untrusted input.
  //   Zod catches this before we get here, but belt + suspenders.
  if (!Number.isFinite(dollars)) {
    throw new RangeError(`Cannot convert ${dollars} to cents`);
  }
  return Math.round(dollars * 100) as CentsAmount;
}

/** Base class for every error the package can produce. */
export abstract class BaseError extends Error {
  abstract readonly code: string;
  /** Structured context safe for logging (never contains PII). */
  abstract readonly context: Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean>>;

  constructor(message: string, options?: ErrorOptions) {
    super(message, options);
    this.name = this.constructor.name;
  }
}

 *   ./reportgen -i sample_sales.csv -g region -a "sum(total),avg(total),count(*)"

// =====================================================================

static std::string str_trim(const std::string& s) {
    size_t a = s.find_first_not_of(" \t\r\n");
    if (a == std::string::npos) return "";
    size_t b = s.find_last_not_of(" \t\r\n");
    return s.substr(a, b - a + 1);
}

static std::string str_lower(std::string s) {
    for (auto& c : s) c = static_cast<char>(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)));
    return s;
}

static bool is_numeric(const std::string& s) {
    if (s.empty()) return false;
    char* end = nullptr;
    std::strtod(s.c_str(), &end);
    return end != s.c_str() && *end == '\0';
}

static double to_double(const std::string& s) {
    try { return std::stod(s); }
    catch (...) { return 0.0; }
}

static std::string now_stamp() {
    std::time_t t = std::time(nullptr);
    char buf[64];
    std::strftime(buf, sizeof buf, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", std::localtime(&t));
    return buf;
}

static std::string fmt_number(double v) {
    if (v == std::floor(v) && std::abs(v) < 1e15)
        return std::to_string(static_cast<long long>(v));
    std::ostringstream os;
    os << std::fixed << std::setprecision(2) << v;
    return os.str();
}

static std::string esc_html(const std::string& s) {
    std::string out;
    out.reserve(s.size());
    for (char c : s)
        switch (c) {
            case '<': out += "<";   break;
            case '>': out += ">";   break;
            case '&': out += "&";  break;
            case '"': out += """; break;
            default:  out += c;
        }
    return out;
}

static std::string esc_json(const std::string& s) {
    std::string out;
    out.reserve(s.size());
    for (char c : s)
        switch (c) {
            case '"':  out += "\\\""; break;
            case '\\': out += "\\\\"; break;
            case '\n': out += "\\n";  break;
            case '\t': out += "\\t";  break;
            default:   out += c;
        }
    return out;
}

static std::string csv_quote(const std::string& s) {
    if (s.find_first_of(",\"\n") == std::string::npos) return s;
    std::string out = "\"";
    for (char c : s) {
        if (c == '"') out += '"';
        out += c;
    }
    return out + '"';
}

# Senior Exercise: Resilient File Sync Engine

## The Prompt Given to Candidates

> Build `filesync`, a dependency-light CLI tool **and** browser-compatible sync engine that keeps a local file tree consistent with a remote REST manifest. Your solution must survive server outages without hammering the origin on recovery, correctly invalidate a stale offline cache, and never corrupt state when multiple async operations overlap.

## API Contract (provided as a stub server)

```javascript
// stub-server.js — run with: node stub-server.js
// Gives candidates a real endpoint to code against.

import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { randomUUID, createHash } from "node:crypto";

const FILES = new Map();
let generation = 1;

function seed() {
  for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) {
    const id = randomUUID();
    const body = Buffer.from(`content-of-${id}-gen-${generation}`);
    FILES.set(id, {
      body,
      etag: createHash("sha256").update(body).digest("hex").slice(0, 16),
      modified: Date.now(),
    });
  }
}
seed();

// Rotate some files every 30 s so caches go stale
setInterval(() => {
  generation++;
  let flipped = 0;
  for (const [id, entry] of FILES) {
    if (Math.random() < 0.2) {
      const body = Buffer.from(`content-of-${id}-gen-${generation}`);
      entry.body = body;
      entry.etag = createHash("sha256").update(body).digest("hex").slice(0, 16);
      entry.modified = Date.now();
      flipped++;
    }
  }
  console.log(`[server] generation ${generation}, rotated ${flipped} files`);
}, 30_000);

createServer((req, res) => {
  // Simulate outages: 503 for 10 s every 60 s
  if (Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) % 60 < 10) {
    res.writeHead(503, { "Retry-After": "5" });
    return res.end();
  }

  const url = new URL(req.url, `http://${req.headers.host}`);

  if (url.pathname === "/api/v1/manifest") {
    const manifest = {};
    for (const [id, f] of FILES) {
      manifest[id] = { etag: f.etag, size: f.body.length, modified: f.modified };
    }
    const payload = JSON.stringify({ generation, files: manifest });
    res.writeHead(200, {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ETag: `"gen-${generation}"`,
    });
    return res.end(payload);
  }

  const fileMatch = url.pathname.match(/^\/api\/v1\/files\/(.+)$/);
  if (fileMatch) {
    const entry = FILES.get(fileMatch[1]);
    if (!entry) { res.writeHead(404); return res.end(); }

    // Conditional GET
    if (req.headers["if-none-match"] === `"${entry.etag}"`) {
      res.writeHead(304);
      return res.end();
    }
    res.writeHead(200, {
      "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream",
      ETag: `"${entry.etag}"`,
      "Content-Length": entry.body.length,
    });
    return res.end(entry.body);
  }

  res.writeHead(404);
  res.end();
}).listen(3001, () => console.log("stub-server on :3001"));
```

```javascript
/**
 * FileManifest: a frozen, value-typed snapshot of every tracked file.
 *
 * TRADEOFF — Memory vs. safety
 * ─────────────────────────────
 * Every `.with*` method allocates a fresh Map + object shell.
 *   • 10 k entries × 10 interim snapshots ≈ 4 MB  — acceptable.
 *   • 1 M entries → switch to a HAMT or delta-encode against a base.
 * We choose safety here: two concurrent sync loops can each hold a
 * manifest reference without one silently mutating the other's view.
 *
 * PITFALL this prevents
 * ─────────────────────
 * Without freezing, a pattern like:
 *   const m = engine.manifest;
 *   await downloadAll(m);          // yields to the event loop
 *   engine.manifest.delete(id);    // someone else mutates mid-loop
 * corrupts the iteration.  Frozen snapshots make this a TypeError.
 */

export class FileManifest {
  /** @type {number} monotonic server generation */
  #generation;

  /** @type {ReadonlyMap<string, Readonly<FileEntry>>} */
  #entries;

  /**
   * @param {number} generation
   * @param {Iterable<[string, FileEntry]>} entries
   */
  constructor(generation, entries) {
    this.#generation = generation;
    this.#entries = Object.freeze(new Map(entries));
    Object.freeze(this);
  }

  get generation() {
    return this.#generation;
  }
  get size() {
    return this.#entries.size;
  }

  get(id) {
    return this.#entries.get(id);
  }

  has(id) {
    return this.#entries.has(id);
  }

  entries() {
    return this.#entries.entries();
  }

  [Symbol.iterator]() {
    return this.#entries[Symbol.iterator]();
  }

  /** Immutable update — returns a new manifest. */
  withEntry(id, entry) {
    const next = new Map(this.#entries);
    next.set(id, Object.freeze({ ...entry }));
    return new FileManifest(this.#generation, next);
  }

  /** Immutable delete. */
  withoutEntry(id) {
    const next = new Map(this.#entries);
    next.delete(id);
    return new FileManifest(this.#generation, next);
  }

  /**
   * Compute the delta needed to go from `this` (local) to `remote`.
   * Returns arrays rather than a generator so callers can `.length`
   * without consuming the iterator — worth the memory for the UX.
   *
   * TRADEOFF: Materialising three arrays costs O(n) memory.
   * A generator-based approach saves memory but loses random access
   * and `.length`. At 50 k files × ~100 bytes/entry = 5 MB, arrays win
   * for usability. Beyond 500 k files, switch to a streaming diff.
   */
  diff(remote) {
    const added = [];   // in remote, not in local
    const changed = []; // in both, different etag
    const removed = []; // in local, not in remote

    for (const [id, remoteEntry] of remote) {
      const localEntry = this.#entries.get(id);

### Why sqlx?
- Compile-time checked SQL queries
- Async-native (works with tokio)
- No ORM overhead - important for security teams who want to see exact SQL
- Supports migrations
- Type-safe without runtime reflection

### Deterministic output order
- Use a sequence number assigned at ingestion
- Process concurrently using a worker pool, then sort by sequence number before persisting to maintain order guarantees even under concurrent load

### Bounded channel backpressure
- Use `tokio::sync::mpsc` with bounded channels
- When the channel is full, producers slow down naturally
- This prevents memory exhaustion under bursty traffic

### Predictable latency
- Bounded channels limit queue depth
- Processing uses a semaphore to limit concurrency
- Timeout on all async operations

# Rust Config Parser for Containerized Session Management

## Architecture Overview

```
┌──────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐      ┌──────────────────┐
│  SQLite       │─────▶│  Lenient      │─────▶│  Drift           │
│  Snapshot     │      │  Parser       │      │  Detector        │
│  Reader       │      │  (partial OK) │      │  (env A vs B)    │
└──────────────┘      └──────┬───────┘      └────────┬─────────┘
                             │                        │
┌──────────────┐      ┌──────▼───────┐      ┌────────▼─────────┐
│  reqwest      │─────▶│  Bounded      │─────▶│  Prometheus      │
│  Remote Fetch │      │  Queue        │      │  Metrics         │
└──────────────┘      └──────────────┘      └──────────────────┘
```

## Failure Modes Reference

| # | Failure | How it surfaces | Recovery |
|---|---------|----------------|----------|
| F1 | SQLite file missing / locked | `ConfigError::SnapshotNotFound` or `Sqlite` with OS error | Caller retries or skips snapshot |
| F2 | Schema mismatch (column renamed) | `ConfigError::SchemaMismatch` with expected vs found | Operator alert; blocks processing |
| F3 | Single row has malformed JSON | `RowOutcome::Failed` in batch; other rows still parse | Partial result returned; error counter incremented |
| F4 | Field inside valid JSON has wrong type | `FieldError` collected; remaining fields still extracted | `PartialSessionConfig` carries what survived |
| F5 | Payload exceeds size limit | `ConfigError::PayloadTooLarge` before deserialisation starts | Row skipped, metric incremented |
| F6 | Remote endpoint unreachable | `ConfigError::Network` wrapping `reqwest::Error` | Timeout + bounded retries in client |
| F7 | Remote returns 4xx/5xx | `ConfigError::HttpStatus` with status code and URL | No retry on 4xx; retry on 5xx |
| F8 | Queue full | `ConfigError::QueueFull` with capacity and current depth | Back-pressure to caller; gauge stays at capacity |
| F9 | Drift between environments | `DriftReport` with per-field diffs and drift score | Logged and counted; not an error unless score > threshold |
| F10 | Session expired in snapshot | `ConfigError::SessionExpired` with ID and timestamp | Row filtered out, not counted as parse error |

use std::path::PathBuf;
use thiserror::Error;

/// Every fallible path produces a typed variant with enough context
/// to debug without a stack trace.  Nothing is hidden behind `.unwrap()`.
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum ConfigError {
    // --- storage --------------------------------------------------------
    #[error("snapshot not found: {0}")]
    SnapshotNotFound(PathBuf),                              // F1

    #[error("sqlite error on {path}: {source}")]
    Sqlite { path: PathBuf, source: rusqlite::Error },      // F1

    #[error("schema mismatch in {path}: want {expected:?}, got {found:?}")]
    SchemaMismatch {                                        // F2
        path: PathBuf,
        expected: Vec<String>,
        found: Vec<String>,
    },

    // --- parse ----------------------------------------------------------
    #[error("json parse error in row {row_id}: {source}")]
    JsonParse { row_id: i64, source: serde_json::Error },   // F3

    #[error("payload too large: {size} bytes > {limit} limit")]
    PayloadTooLarge { size: usize, limit: usize },          // F5

    #[error("session expired: id={session_id}")]
    SessionExpired { session_id: String },                  // F10

    // --- network --------------------------------------------------------
    #[error("network error fetching {url}: {source}")]
    Network { url: String, source: reqwest::Error },        // F6

    #[error("HTTP {status} from {url}")]
    HttpStatus { url: String, status: u16 },                // F7

    // --- pipeline -------------------------------------------------------
    #[error("queue full: capacity={capacity}, depth={depth}")]
    QueueFull { capacity: usize, depth: usize },            // F8

    #[error("unknown environment: {0}")]
    UnknownEnvironment(String),
}

/// Tracks a single field that could not be deserialised inside an
/// otherwise-valid JSON object.  Collected, never panicked on.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct FieldError {
    pub field: String,
    pub detail: String,
}

impl FieldError {
    pub fn new(field: impl Into<String>, err: impl std::fmt::Display) -> Self {
        Self { field: field.into(), detail: err.to_string() }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for FieldError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "field '{}': {}", self.field, self.detail)
    }
}

```rust
use prometheus::{
    Histogram, HistogramOpts, IntCounter, IntGauge, Opts, Registry,
};

/// All counters/gauges live here.  Cloned handles are `Arc` internally
/// so passing `Metrics` across threads is cheap.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Metrics {
    pub parse_success_total:  IntCounter,
    pub parse_error_total:    IntCounter,
    pub parse_partial_total:  IntCounter,   // full JSON ok, some fields bad
    pub queue_depth:          IntGauge,
    pub drift_detected_total: IntCounter,
    pub fetch_success_total:  IntCounter,
    pub fetch_error_total:    IntCounter,
    pub parse_duration_secs:  Histogram,
    pub payload_bytes:        Histogram,
}

impl Metrics {
    /// Registers every metric with `registry`.  Returns an error
    /// (not a panic) if names collide—possible in tests that reuse
    /// the global registry.
    pub fn register(registry: &Registry) -> Result<Self, prometheus::Error> {
        macro_rules! counter {
            ($name:expr, $help:expr) => {{
                let c = IntCounter::with_opts(Opts::new($name, $help))?;
                registry.register(Box::new(c.clone()))?;
                c
            }};
        }

        let queue_depth = IntGauge::with_opts(
            Opts::new("config_queue_depth", "Jobs waiting in the processing queue"),
        )?;
        registry.register(Box::new(queue_depth.clone()))?;

        let parse_duration_secs = Histogram::with_opts(
            HistogramOpts::new(
                "config_parse_duration_seconds",
                "Wall-clock time to parse one config blob",
            )
            .buckets(vec![0.0001, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1]),
        )?;
        registry.register(Box::new(parse_duration_secs.clone()))?;

        let payload_bytes = Histogram::with_opts(
            HistogramOpts::new("config_payload_bytes", "Size of raw config blobs")
                .buckets(prometheus::exponential_buckets(256.0, 4.0, 8)?),
        )?;
        registry.register(Box::new(payload_bytes.clone()))?;

        Ok(Self {
            parse_success_total:  counter!("config_parse_success_total",  "Blobs fully parsed"),
            parse_error_total:    counter!("config_parse_error_total",    "Blobs that failed entirely"),
            parse_partial_total:  counter!("config_parse_partial_total",  "Blobs parsed with field errors"),
            drift_detected_total: counter!("config_drift_detected_total", "Drift events between envs"),
            fetch_success_total:  counter!("config_fetch_success_total",  "Remote fetches ok"),
            fetch_error_total:    counter!("config_fetch_error_total",    "Remote fetches failed"),
            queue_depth,
            parse_duration_secs,
            payload_bytes,
        })
    }

    /// Render all metrics in Prometheus text exposition format.
    /// Returns `String` instead of writing to stdout so callers can
    /// serve it from any HTTP handler.
    pub fn render(&self, registry: &Registry) -> String {
        use prometheus::Encoder;
        let encoder = prometheus::TextEncoder::new();
        let families = registry.gather();
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        // encode only fails on I/O errors on a Vec, which won't happen
        encoder.encode(&families, &mut buf).expect("vec write is infallible");
        String::from_utf8(buf).expect("prometheus output is valid utf-8")
    }
}

# Production Task-Scheduling Cache in Rust

## Architecture Overview & Why `reqwest`

The system sits between external CSV export endpoints and an internal task scheduler. The cache avoids repeated fetches from slow upstream sources.

**Why `reqwest`:**
- Streams response bodies via `bytes_stream()` — critical for large CSV payloads that shouldn't be fully buffered before parsing begins
- Connection-pooling through its internal `Client` (backed by `hyper`) — a single `Client` instance reuses TCP/TLS connections across fetches
- Per-request and per-connection timeouts — you need distinct connect vs. read timeouts in a tooling context where upstream services are unreliable
- The alternative space: `hyper` is too low-level (manual connection management), `ureq` is blocking-only, `surf` has a thinner ecosystem. `reqwest` hits the right abstraction level for an application-layer HTTP client

**Key architectural constraint:** domain types and scheduling logic import *nothing* from `reqwest`, `csv`, or `dashmap`. Swapping any infrastructure crate touches only its adapter module.

```text
                  ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │         Orchestrator (lib.rs)          │
                  │  wires fetch → parse → cache → schedule│
                  └────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────────┘
                       │          │          │

### config/index.js — Schema-Validated Config Factory

```js
// config/index.js
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// KEY RULE: this module exports a *function*, not a frozen object.
// Every call returns an independent copy, so parallel tests never
// collide and containers can reload config without restarting.
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
'use strict';

const Ajv = require('ajv');

const schema = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['queue', 'server'],
  additionalProperties: false,
  properties: {
    server: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        host:  { type: 'string',  default: '0.0.0.0' },
        port:  { type: 'integer', default: 3000, minimum: 1, maximum: 65535 },
      },
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
    queue: {
      type: 'object',
      required: ['url'],
      properties: {
        url:                 { type: 'string', minLength: 1 },
        concurrency:         { type: 'integer', default: 5, minimum: 1, maximum: 50 },
        batchSize:           { type: 'integer', default: 5, minimum: 1, maximum: 10 },
        maxRetries:          { type: 'integer', default: 3, minimum: 0 },
        retryBaseMs:         { type: 'integer', default: 1_000, minimum: 0 },
        pollIntervalMs:      { type: 'integer', default: 5_000, minimum: 100 },
        pollBackoffMs:       { type: 'integer', default: 10_000, minimum: 100 },
        dedupWindowMs:       { type: 'integer', default: 300_000, minimum: 1_000 },
        visibilityTimeoutMs: { type: 'integer', default: 60_000, minimum: 1_000 },
      },
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
    storage: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        endpoint: { type: 'string', default: '' },
        bucket:   { type: 'string', default: 'processed' },
      },
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
    logger: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        level: { type: 'string', default: 'info',
                 enum: ['fatal','error','warn','info','debug','trace','silent'] },
      },
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  },
};

/**
 * Pure factory. Accepts an optional env map so tests never
 * mutate `process.env`.  Returns a deeply-frozen config.
 *
 * @param {{ env?: Record<string,string>, overrides?: object }} opts
 */
function loadConfig({ env = process.env, overrides = {} } = {}) {
  // 1. Map environment variables to structure
  const fromEnv = {
    server: {
      host: env.HOST,
      port: env.PORT ? Number(env.PORT) : undefined,
    },
    queue: {
      url:            env.QUEUE_URL,
      concurrency:    env.QUEUE_CONCURRENCY    ? Number(env.QUEUE_CONCURRENCY) : undefined,
      batchSize:      env.QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE     ? Number(env.QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE)  : undefined,
      maxRetries:     env.QUEUE_MAX_RETRIES    ? Number(env.QUEUE_MAX_RETRIES) : undefined,
      retryBaseMs:    env.QUEUE_RETRY_BASE_MS  ? Number(env.QUEUE_RETRY_BASE_MS) : undefined,
      pollIntervalMs: env.QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL  ? Number(env.QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL)  : undefined,
    },
    storage: {
      endpoint: env.STORAGE_ENDPOINT,
      bucket:   env.STORAGE_BUCKET,
    },
    logger: {
      level: env.LOG_LEVEL,
    },
  };

  // 2. Two-level merge: env ← overrides  (overrides win)
  const merged = {};
  for (const section of Object.keys(schema.properties)) {
    merged[section] = {
      ...stripUndefined(fromEnv[section] ?? {}),
      ...stripUndefined(overrides[section] ?? {}),
    };
  }

  // 3. Validate (ajv fills in defaults from the schema)
  const ajv = new Ajv({ useDefaults: true, coerceTypes: true });
  const validate = ajv.compile(schema);
  if (!validate(merged)) {
    const msgs = validate.errors.map(
      (e) => `  ${e.instancePath || '/'} ${e.message}`,
    );
    throw new TypeError(`Invalid configuration:\n${msgs.join('\n')}`);
  }

  return deepFreeze(merged);
}

// ── helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function stripUndefined(obj) {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(obj).filter(([, v]) => v !== undefined),
  );
}

function deepFreeze(obj) {
  if (obj && typeof obj === 'object') {
    Object.values(obj).forEach(deepFreeze);
  }
  return Object.freeze(obj);
}

module.exports = { loadConfig, schema };

### lib/semaphore.js — Bounded Concurrency (Prevent Fan-Out)

```js
// lib/semaphore.js
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// PITFALL THIS SOLVES:
//   messages.map(m => handle(m))       ← unbounded Promise fan-out
//   Promise.all(messages.map(…))       ← same problem, hides OOM
//

        try
        {
            // Wait up to 50 ms then return null (simulates empty-queue poll).
            using var timeout = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(50));
            using var linked  = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct, timeout.Token);

        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            return null;
        }
    }

    public Task AcknowledgeAsync(string messageId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        Acknowledged.Add(messageId);
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }

    public Task RejectAsync(string messageId, TimeSpan retryAfter, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        Rejected.Add((messageId, retryAfter));
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}

// ─── Bounded-cardinality metrics ─────────────────────────────

// BoundedMetrics tracks per-label counters up to maxCardinality
// distinct labels. New labels beyond the cap are folded into
// "__overflow__" so the map cannot grow without bound.
//
// Why this matters:
//   Session IDs are high-cardinality (one per session). Naive
//   map[sessionID]count grows proportionally to sessions seen.
//   Over hours of background processing this can balloon to
//   millions of keys, consuming significant memory. Capping the
//   map at 10,000 labels keeps it bounded to roughly 800 KB
//   worst case, with overflow events still counted accurately
//   even if per-label granularity is lost.
//
// Alternatives considered:
//   • HyperLogLog for distinct count — loses per-label totals.
//   • Count-Min Sketch — probabilistic, harder to debug.
//   • LRU eviction — better precision but more complex.
//   • External push (Prometheus) — not available in all CLI
//     deployments.
//
// For an internal CLI, cap-and-overflow is the simplest choice.

type BoundedMetrics struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	labels map[string]*atomic.Int64
	card   int

	FilesOK   atomic.Int64
	FilesErr  atomic.Int64
	BytesRead atomic.Int64
}

func newMetrics() *BoundedMetrics {
	return &BoundedMetrics{
		labels: make(map[string]*atomic.Int64, 256),
	}
}

func (m *BoundedMetrics) Inc(label string) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	ctr, ok := m.labels[label]
	if !ok {
		if m.card >= maxCardinality {
			label = "__overflow__"
			ctr, ok = m.labels[label]
		}
		if !ok {
			ctr = &atomic.Int64{}
			m.labels[label] = ctr
			m.card++
		}
	}
	m.mu.Unlock()
	ctr.Add(1)
